To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BOB, P BOB and LMP BOB are efficient data structures for implementing dynamic router tables with nonintersecting rule filters and with the highest-priority matching tie breaker.

BOB, P BOB and LMP BOB are all O(log n) data structures for dynamic router tables with nonintersecting range filters and highest-priority matching and that BOB, LMPBOB and PBOB all perform search, insert, delete in O(log n) and have O(log n) misses.

BOB, P, LMPBOB, PBOBO, and LMPBOBO are the first data structures that perform all three operations - insert, delete and lookup - in O(log n) expected time and with O (log n) expected cache misses for n rule filters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
dynamic routing tables that are updated in response to changes in the network.
the design and analysis of dynamic router tables in the context of the Internet and the World Wide Web.

developing a dynamic router table data structure for the case of highest priority matching, and with developing modified version of this data structure for the cases of prefix matching and longest prefix matching.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for dynamic router tables with highest-priority matching, BOB, LMPBOB and PBOB are the most practical data structures.
the BOB data structure is an excellent data structure for dynamic router tables.
BOB is the most general and most efficient data structure for dynamic router tables with highest-priority tie breaking.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

BOB, P-BOB and LMB-BOB are the best data structures for dynamic router tables with nonintersecting ranges, prefixes, or longest-prefix matching, and they are the best for the highest priority tie breaker.
BOB, P-BOB and L-BOB are efficient data structures to implement router tables in which rule filters are non-intersecting ranges and in particular, in the special case when rule filters are prefixes.

BOB is a general purpose dynamic router-table data structure for nonintersecting range filters and the highest-priority matching tie breaker and PBOB and LMBOB are special purpose data structures for prefixes with longest-prefix matching and highest-priority matching, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamic router table problem is not a difficult problem.
the highest-priority match is a good default choice for dynamic router table design.
dynamic router tables can be made to run fast by using a data structure that does not use any kind of hashing.
